ican: I can identify the driver gear and the driven gear.
I can state the direction of rotation of each gear.
I can describe the function of an idler gear.
I can draw a gear train using the correct conventions.
I can calculate velocity ratio from input and output speeds.

cloze.title: Say it the exam way
cloze.text:
The gear on the input shaft is the [[driver|driven|idler]] gear. The gear on the output shaft is the [[driven|driver|idler]] gear. Two meshing gears turn in [[opposite|the same]] directions.

An idler gear makes the driver and driven gears turn in the [[same|opposite]] direction. It has [[no effect|a big effect]] on the output speed.

Velocity ratio = speed of input ÷ speed of [[output|input]]. Velocity ratio has [[no unit|the unit revs min⁻¹]]. Give the ratio in its [[simplest|longest]] form, such as 5 : 2.

Gears are drawn with [[solid|dashed]] lines, a double outline and a [[cross|dot]] at the centre.

check.q: State the name of the gear on the input shaft.
A driver gear turns clockwise. State the direction of the driven gear it meshes with.

check.a: It makes the driver and the driven gear turn in the same direction.

check.q: A simple gear train has an input speed of 600 revs min⁻¹ and an output speed of 200 revs min⁻¹. Calculate the velocity ratio.
check.a: VR = speed of input ÷ speed of output = 600 ÷ 200 = 3 : 1

check.q: State two conventions used to draw gears.
check.a: Any two: solid lines; two circles (a double outline); a cross at the centre.

check.q: State the name of the gear on the output shaft.
State the effect of an idler gear on the output speed.
check.a: No effect: the output speed does not change.

paper2.alt: A motorised coffee grinder uses a simple gear train. A small driver gear turns at 260 revs per minute and a large driven gear turns at 104 revs per minute. (a) Calculate the velocity ratio of the gear train. Show all working and final unit. 2 marks. (b) Describe how the simple gear drive could be altered to make the driver and driven gears turn in the same direction. 1 mark.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2015 Section 1, Question 4. (a) VR = 260 / 104 = 2.5 (2.5 : 1, 5 : 2 and so on). 1 mark for substitution, 1 mark for the answer; ignore any units. (b) An extra gear between the driver and driven, or use an idler gear. Do not accept just add another gear without saying where it should be added.

paper2.lead: Build It D2 in your booklet (the coffee grinder) is based on this question.

paper2.alt: A diagram of part of a gear mechanism for an electric food mixer is shown below: input gear A meshes with a small gear B, which meshes with a large output gear C. (a)(i) State the name of gear B. 1 mark. (ii) Describe the function of gear B. 1 mark. (b) Calculate the velocity ratio when input A rotates at 1200 revs per minute and output C has a speed of 720 revs per minute. Show all working. 2 marks.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2016 Question 6. (a)(i) Idler. (ii) It makes gear A and gear C turn in the same direction, without affecting the output speed; accept change the output direction; not keep the direction the same on its own. (b) VR = speed of input / speed of output = 1200 / 720 = 5 : 3 or 1.7 : 1. 1 mark for substitution, 1 mark for the answer.

paper2.alt: A simple gear train used in a winch system is shown below. Input gear A turns at 990 revs per minute; it meshes with gear B, which meshes with output gear C turning at 66 revs per minute. (a)(i) State the name of gear B. (ii) State the effect of gear B on the output speed. (b) Calculate the velocity ratio of the gear train.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2017 Question 7. (a)(i) Idler. (ii) No effect. (b) Velocity ratio = speed of input / speed of output = 990 / 66 = 15 : 1. 1 mark for substitution, 1 mark for the answer. Accept just 15; ignore any units.

paper2.alt: The diagram below represents a simple gear train: a driver gear and a driven gear with a small gear X between them. (a) State the name of gear X. 1 mark. (b) Describe the purpose of gear X in this simple gear train. 1 mark.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for the specimen paper Question 4. (a) Idler gear. (b) It makes the driver and driven turn the same way. Do not accept that it has no effect on the speed of the gears.

paper2.alt: The simple gear train shown below has been drawn using incorrect conventions: two meshing gears drawn as single dashed circles with a dot at each centre. Describe two errors that were made when drawing this simple gear train. 2 marks.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2018 Question 8. Any two: incorrect line type used, not solid lines; should be crosses in the centres, not dots; double outlines missing. Must be descriptive. Do not accept overlapping or lines incorrect.

paper2.alt: A simple gear train is shown below. The driver turns at 800 revs per minute and the driven gear at 320 revs per minute. (a) Calculate the velocity ratio of this simple gear train. 2 marks. The driver gear rotates clockwise. (b) State the direction of rotation of the driven gear. 1 mark.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2019 Question 4. (a) Velocity ratio = speed of input / speed of output = 800 / 320 = 5 : 2. Accept 2.5 : 1 or 2.5; ignore any units. (b) Anticlockwise. Do not accept other way or opposite way. Accept the direction shown on the diagram.

paper2.alt: A gear train is shown below: three meshing gears drawn as double circles with centre crosses; the middle gear is labelled A. (a) State the type of gear train shown. 1 mark. (b) State the name of gear A. 1 mark.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2022 Question 1. (a) Simple. (b) Idler.

paper2.alt: A child's game is shown. A diagram of the simple gear train inside the game shows an input speed of 360 revs per minute and an output speed of 12 revs per minute. Calculate the velocity ratio of this simple gear train. 2 marks.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2023 Question 2. Velocity ratio = speed of input / speed of output = 360 / 12. VR = 30 : 1. 1 mark for substitution, 1 mark for the answer. Ignore any units. Ratio must be simplified. Accept 30.

paper2.alt: A diagram of a simple gear train is shown below. Gear A is the input at 120 revs per minute; it meshes with a small gear B, which meshes with gear C, the output at 820 revs per minute. (a) Calculate the velocity ratio of this simple gear train. 2 marks. (b) State the effect on the output velocity if the number of teeth on gear B is reduced. 1 mark.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2024 Question 4. (a) Velocity ratio = speed of input / speed of output = 120 / 820 = 6 / 41. VR = 6 : 41. Ignore any unit. Accept 1 : 6.8, 0.15 : 1 or 0.146. Ratio must be simplified. (b) No effect. The velocity of gear C will not change.

errors: Simplify the ratio: 360 ÷ 12 gives 30 : 1. The marking says the ratio must be simplified (2023, 2024).
Name the direction: anticlockwise. "Other way" or "opposite way" got no mark (2019).
Say what an idler does: it makes the driver and driven gears turn the same way. "It has no effect on the speed" got no mark (2017 specimen).
Say where a new gear goes: between the driver and the driven gear. "Add another gear" alone got no mark (2015).
Draw gears with solid lines, a double outline and a cross at each centre, not a dot (2018).
